content.intro: This lesson covers Custom Number Formats as part of Cell Formatting and Spreadsheet Design. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Custom Number Formats establishes the workbook structure and data-quality habits that later formulas and reports depend on. A clear layout reduces avoidable editing mistakes and makes the workbook easier for another person to understand.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Test values just below, exactly at and above each threshold. Keep business rules visible and avoid nesting many IF functions when a lookup table is easier to audit.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for custom number formats. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates custom number formats. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.

At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
